page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a nominal clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores across 2 threads per core, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU footprint. The instance includes hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, AES, and SHA vector and cryptographic extensions. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, while external connectivity features a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without included public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that single-threaded performance lands within average mid-tier expectations, marked by a stress-ng single-core score of 1858.18 and gzip compression reaching 27.56 GB/s. In contrast, multi-threaded CPU capabilities place lower, with a stress-ng multi-core metric of 3853.92 and PassMark CPU rating of 5887.68. Memory tests demonstrate moderate performance, recording a PassMark memory score of 2387.77, though large block uncached read and write bandwidth register at 30.29 GB/s and 25.91 GB/s respectively. Redis throughput attains 3.99 million SET operations per second, while static web serving delivers 6.41 GB/s and lightweight 135M LLM text generation operates at 103.36 tokens per second.

Given its high RAM allocation relative to compute cores, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for architectures needing substantial memory residency without paying for excess compute capacity. However, multi-core throughput and raw memory bandwidth represent explicit tradeoffs that limit sustained parallel compute tasks. Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive caching servers, in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning modules, and mid-tier backend services operating against network storage.
